symbols.name: \(Y_n(a)\)
symbols.def: Potential outcome under treatment state \(a\) on a causal extension.

symbols.name: \(\Gamma(\nu_0,\nu_1)\)
symbols.def: Set of couplings with marginals \(\nu_0\) and \(\nu_1\).

symbols.name: \(u_{a,n}\)
symbols.def: An optimal conditional quadratic Kantorovich dual potential for \(Q_{a,P_n}\).

symbols.name: \(J_n\)
symbols.def: Wavelet or sieve resolution satisfying \(2^{J_nD}\asymp n^{D/(2s+D)}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat q_{a,-k,n}\)
symbols.def: Normalized fitted arm density satisfying \(\int_{\mathcal Y}\widehat q_{a,-k,n}(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)=1\) for almost every \(x\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat V_{-k,n}\)
symbols.def: Plug-in conditional transport value from the fitted arm kernels.

symbols.name: \(r_{\phi,n}\)
symbols.def: Centered-potential rate derived from \(r_{q,n}\) by the proposed transport-stability argument.

symbols.name: \(r_{V,n}\)
symbols.def: Conditional-transport-value rate derived from \(r_{q,n}\) by the proposed transport-stability argument.

assumptions.condition: \(c\le q_{a,n}(x,y)\le C\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \((x,y)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\).
\(\phi_{a,n}(x,\cdot)+\lVert\cdot\rVert_2^2/2\) is \(\lambda\)-strongly convex for every \((x,a)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal A\).

\(\mathcal X\) is the closure of a bounded connected Lipschitz domain in \(\mathbb R^{d_X}\), and \(\mathcal Y\) is the closure of a bounded connected uniformly convex \(C^2\) domain with nonempty interior in \(\mathbb R^{d_Y}\).

novel.justification: standard: connected-support first variation in Manole et al. (2024), Lemma 23, and standard global Brenier regularity on uniformly convex domains

assumptions.condition: Let \(\mathfrak F\) be the feasible conditional-density class in the corrected \(def:coupled-fold-learners\). There exist fixed constants \(0<m_{\mathrm{OT}}\le M_{\mathrm{OT}}<\infty\) such that, for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\) and almost every \(x\), the quadratic Brenier potential \(b_{f_0,f_1,x}\) transporting \(f_0(x,\cdot)\) to \(f_1(x,\cdot)\) belongs to \(C^2(\mathcal Y)\) and satisfies \[m_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\preceq\nabla_y^2b_{f_0,f_1,x}(y)\preceq M_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\quad\text{for every }y\in\mathcal Y.\]

novel.justification: standard: the uniform form of the \(A1(\lambda)\) curvature condition in Manole et al. (2024), Theorem 6, justified by global Caffarelli regularity under suitable smooth positive densities and regular domains

assumptions.condition: With \(\mathfrak F\) denoting the feasible conditional-density class in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\), the quadratic Brenier potential \(b_{f_0,f_1,x}\) transporting \(f_0(x,\cdot)\) to \(f_1(x,\cdot)\) belongs to \(C^2(\mathcal Y)\) for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\) and almost every \(x\).

There exists a fixed constant \(m_{\mathrm{OT}}>0\) such that \(\nabla_y^2 b_{f_0,f_1,x}(y)\succeq m_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\) for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\), almost every \(x\), and every \(y\in\mathcal Y\).

standard.name: uniform A1-type lower Brenier curvature, manole2024plugin

assumptions.condition: There exists a fixed constant \(M_{\mathrm{OT}}<\infty\) such that \(\nabla_y^2 b_{f_0,f_1,x}(y)\preceq M_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\) for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\), almost every \(x\), and every \(y\in\mathcal Y\).

standard.name: uniform A1-type upper Brenier curvature, manole2024plugin

assumptions.condition: There exist fixed constants \(t_\pi,L_\pi>0\) such that \(\pi_n\in\Sigma(t_\pi,L_\pi;\mathcal X)\) and \(\varepsilon\le\pi_n(x)\le1-\varepsilon\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\).

definitions.name: Smooth observed-law parent class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{P_n\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times\mathcal A\times\mathcal Y):P_n\text{ satisfies }ass:fixed-overlap,ass:compact-support,ass:bounded-arm-densities,ass:holder-arm-densities\}\). No lower bound is imposed on \(\sigma_n^2\); in particular, \(\sigma_n^2=0\) is permitted whenever the displayed member properties hold.

definitions.name: Normalized coupled foldwise transport learners
definitions.construction: Choose deterministic folds satisfying \(\max_{1\le k\le K}||I_{k,n}|-n/K|\le1\). Let \(\mathfrak F\) be the class of \(f\in\Sigma(s,L;\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)\) such that \(c\le f\le C\) and \(\int_{\mathcal Y}f(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)=1\) for almost every \(x\). Let \(\mathfrak F_{J_n}\) be a fixed finite \(L^\infty\)-net of \(\mathfrak F\), constructed by quantizing boundary-adapted tensor-wavelet coefficients through level \(J_n\), with mesh order \(2^{-J_ns}\) and logarithmic cardinality order \(2^{J_nD}\). Put \(N_{a,-k,n}=\sum_{j\notin I_{k,n}}1\{A_{j,n}=a\}\). If \(N_{a,-k,n}>0\), define \(\widehat q_{a,-k,n}\) as the lexicographically first minimizer over \(f\in\mathfrak F_{J_n}\) of \[\frac1{N_{a,-k,n}}\sum_{j\notin I_{k,n}:A_{j,n}=a}\left\{\int_{\mathcal Y}f(X_{j,n},y)^2d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)-2f(X_{j,n},Y_{j,n})\right\}.\] If \(N_{a,-k,n}=0\), use the first element of \(\mathfrak F_{J_n}\). For every \(k,n\), fix before observing the data a rule \(\mathsf A_{\pi,k,n}\) such that \((t,x)\mapsto\mathsf A_{\pi,k,n}(t)(x)\in(0,1)\) is jointly measurable for a training sample \(t\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\). Set \(\widehat\pi_{-k,n}=\mathsf A_{\pi,k,n}(\mathcal T_{-k,n})\), set \(\bar\pi_{-k,n}=\min\{1-\varepsilon,\max\{\varepsilon,\widehat\pi_{-k,n}\}\}\), and define \(\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(B\mid x)=\int_B\widehat q_{a,-k,n}(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)\). Select the conditional quadratic optimizer and a mutually \(c\)-conjugate dual pair measurably by the minimum-norm normalized tie-break, obtaining \(x\mapsto\widehat\gamma_{-k,n}(\cdot\mid x)\) and \(x\mapsto(\widehat u_{0,-k,n},\widehat u_{1,-k,n})\). Require dual feasibility, contact on \(\widehat\gamma_{-k,n}\), and \(\widehat V_{-k,n}(x)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\widehat u_{a,-k,n}(x,y)\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(dy\mid x)\). Finally set \(\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}=\widehat u_{a,-k,n}-\int\widehat u_{a,-k,n}d\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}\), so its fitted-kernel mean is exactly zero.

definitions.name: Foldwise Hölder and propensity rate route
definitions.construction: Use the finite-net conditional-density empirical-risk minimizer in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\) with \(2^{J_nD}\asymp n^{D/(2s+D)}\). Define \(r_{q,n}=n^{-s/(2s+D)}\), \(r_{\phi,n}=r_{q,n}\), \(r_{V,n}=r_{q,n}\), \(r_{S,n}=r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}\), and \(r_{\sigma,n}=r_{S,n}+n^{-1/2}\). The density rate is derived from approximation error \(2^{-J_ns}\), entropy \(\log|\mathfrak F_{J_n}|\lesssim2^{J_nD}\), and the empirical conditional-density loss. The transport-potential, value, signed quadratic-remainder, score, and variance rates are conclusions derived from the three all-feasible-pairs Brenier assumptions, dual contact, exact centering, and cross-fitting. No propensity smoothness or propensity rate is part of this density route.

definitions.name: Empirical score studentizer
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\sigma_n^2=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i\in I_{k,n}}[\widehat S_{-k,n}(O_{i,n})-\widehat\theta_n]^2\) and \(\widehat\sigma_n=(\widehat\sigma_n^2)^{1/2}\). In every studentized statistic in this core, define a quotient with denominator \(\widehat\sigma_n=0\) to equal zero.

definitions.name: Second-order conditional-transport handle
definitions.construction: Derive second conditional Brenier derivatives along local perturbations of \(Q_{0,P_n}\) and \(Q_{1,P_n}\), then combine their observed-data scores with a derivative-aware resampling rule.

definitions.name: Predetermined triangular law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr P=\{\mathbf P=(P_n)_{n\ge1}:\text{for every }n,\ O_{1,n},\ldots,O_{n,n}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P_n,\ P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}},\text{ and the support-geometry and three all-feasible-pairs conditional Brenier conditions hold}\}\). This complete-sequence class is fixed before observing any data and is not defined by coverage, asymptotic linearity, a remainder rate, or any conclusion of Theorem 2. Uniformity at row \(n\) means \(\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P}P_n(\cdot)\).

definitions.name: Generic and primitive propensity-rate regimes
definitions.construction:
Fix before observing data a jointly measurable learner rule on every training complement and a deterministic sequence \(r_{\pi,n}\to0\). The generic maintained learner condition is
\[
\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P}
P_n\!\left(\max_k\lVert\bar\pi_{-k,n}-\pi_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n})}>Mr_{\pi,n}\right)=0.
\]
This is an estimator-side hypothesis and does not define membership in \(\mathscr P\). For the primitive H\"older regime, let \(\mathfrak G_{J}\) be a deterministic finite \(L^\infty\)-net of \(\{g\in\Sigma(t_\pi,L_\pi;\mathcal X):\varepsilon\le g\le1-\varepsilon\}\), with mesh \(2^{-Jt_\pi}\) and \(\log|\mathfrak G_J|\lesssim2^{Jd_X}\). On each training complement choose the lexicographically first minimizer of \(\sum_j(A_{j,n}-g(X_{j,n}))^2\) over \(g\in\mathfrak G_J\), and clip it to \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), with \(2^{Jd_X}\asymp n^{d_X/(2t_\pi+d_X)}\).

statements.statement: Under \(ass:consistency\), \(ass:ignorability\), \(ass:fixed-overlap\), and \(ass:regular-support-geometry\), \(Q_{a,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)=\mu_{a,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)\) for \(P_{X,n}\)-almost every \(x\) and every \(a\in\mathcal A\). Thus \(\theta_n\) is the observed-law representation of the known sharp conditional-coupling lower endpoint on \(E[\lVert Y_n(1)-Y_n(0)\rVert_2^2]\). Over \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), at laws satisfying \(ass:regular-support-geometry\), \(\psi_n\) is the canonical gradient of \(\theta_n\) in the nonparametric observed-data model and \(\sigma_n^2\) is its semiparametric efficiency bound.
statements.justification: The theorem separates the causal sharp lower endpoint from its observed-law representation and derives the inverse-propensity canonical gradient by a direct integrated-DQM calculation for every regular observed-data score.
statements.gap: Randomized marginal-sample transport limits do not supply the observational tangent decomposition, its covariate-composition term, or its inverse-propensity arm terms.
statements.consumer: It supplies the semiparametric efficiency benchmark and the influence function used by the cross-fitted one-step estimator.

statements.statement: Does there exist an honest, degeneracy-adaptive confidence procedure uniformly over the full frozen nonparametric conditional-transport class allowing \(\sigma_n\to0\), including exact equality, that is first-order efficient away from equality and correctly second-order calibrated at equality; and which uniform second-derivative, compactness, and spectral conditions are necessary and sufficient?
statements.justification: The broad adaptive question remains open after the exact degeneracy characterization and the route-specific spectral obstruction.
statements.gap: No construction here spans regular positive-variance sequences, arbitrary vanishing variance, and exact equality uniformly over the full parent.
statements.consumer: A solution would govern uncertainty reporting when the conditional-OT endpoint is nearly or exactly degenerate.

sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment under consistency and conditional ignorability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On each training complement, a constrained jointly measurable conditional-density wavelet or sieve produces normalized arm densities bounded in \([c,C]\); a propensity is clipped to \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\). A deterministic measurable conditional-OT selection then generates the value, duals, and fitted-kernel-centered potentials from that same pair. Out-of-fold coupled scores define both estimator and empirical variance.

tldr:
Under consistency, conditional ignorability, and overlap, \(\theta_n=E_{P_n}[W_2^2(Q_{0,P_n}(\cdot\mid X_n),Q_{1,P_n}(\cdot\mid X_n))]\) is the sharp conditional-coupling lower endpoint for \(E[\lVert Y_n(1)-Y_n(0)\rVert_2^2]\).  Its observed-data canonical gradient is
\[
\psi_n(O)=V_n(X)-\theta_n+\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}\frac{1\{A=a\}}{\pi_{a,n}(X)}\phi_{a,n}(X,Y),
\]
with efficiency bound \(\sigma_n^2=E_{P_n}[\psi_n^2]\).  For any predetermined \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\) on which the displayed density and propensity learner rates hold, the explicit cross-fitted coupled wavelet--Brenier one-step estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) and studentizer \(\widehat\sigma_n\) satisfy
\[
\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}\Rightarrow N(0,1)
\]
uniformly over \(\mathscr C\), attain the efficiency bound, and give two-sided Wald coverage tending uniformly to \(1-\alpha\).  The variance-unrestricted parent \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\) remains separate and permits equality.  At equality the first-order gradient vanishes; the proved spectral theorem obstructs only the unregularized \(n\)-scale full-tangent Gaussian calibration route.  A broadly honest degeneracy-adaptive procedure, including slower regularized or other derivative-aware constructions, remains open.

project_justification.gap: Lin--Gao--Blanchet--Glynn, arXiv:2602.20681, Theorem 3.2 gives pointwise quadratic-COT asymptotic normality for randomized marginal samples, not the observational tangent-space gradient.  Their arXiv:2506.00257v2/AISTATS 2026 Theorem 6 already treats unconfounded covariate-dependent assignment with two-fold cross-fitting and cellwise self-normalized propensity weighting, but proves a finite-sample expected absolute value-rate for a direct adapted-empirical COT estimator.  It does not give the observed-data canonical gradient, the efficiency bound, root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity, uniform studentized normality, variance consistency, or Wald coverage established here under variance separation.  Ji--Lei--Spector Theorem 3.5 provides observational AIPW validity for fitted dual bounds under two robustness regimes, a distinct inferential construction.
project_justification.niche: The note studies semiparametric estimation and inference for the smooth quadratic conditional-OT lower endpoint in one i.i.d. observational sample.  Identification is supplied by consistency, ignorability, overlap, and conditional-coupling sharpness; the contribution is the observational canonical gradient, efficiency benchmark, coupled one-step expansion, and variance-separated uniform Wald theorem.
project_justification.fill: The analysis derives \(\psi_n\) by a direct integrated-DQM argument over the full nonparametric observed-data tangent space, constructs the explicit propensity-corrected cross-fitted density--Brenier score, proves the exact signed transport remainder and propensity product bias, supplies the primitive elbow \(t_\pi>Dd_X/(4s)\), and separates \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\), \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\), and \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs,H}}_{\sigma_\star,t_\pi,L_\pi}\).  It also proves a route-specific spectral obstruction at equality while keeping the broad adaptive-inference problem open.

related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's arXiv:2602.20681 Theorem 3.2 is the pointwise randomized-marginal comparator for smooth quadratic-COT asymptotic normality.  Their earlier covariate-aware work, arXiv:2502.01164, supplies identification and tightening motivation rather than the observed-data efficiency calculation.  Their arXiv:2506.00257v2/AISTATS Theorem 6 is an observational comparator: under unconfounded covariate-dependent assignment it uses two-fold cross-fitting, cellwise self-normalized inverse-propensity weights, and a discretized adapted-empirical direct COT value estimator; under its average weight-error condition with \(r=1/(d_Z+2\vee d_Y)\), it proves an expected absolute error bound of the form \(C^\dagger\gamma_{d_Y,d_Z}(n_0\wedge n_1)\).  That is a consistency/finite-sample value-rate result, not an observed-data EIF, efficiency, uniform root-\(n\) studentization, variance-consistency, or Wald-coverage result.  Ji, Lei, and Spector Theorem 3.5 establishes observational AIPW validity for fitted dual bounds under its two robustness regimes; their 401(k) SIPP analysis is the applied consumer motivating the present endpoint.  Manole and coauthors motivate the all-feasible-pairs Brenier regularity used for transport stability, while Newey--Robins and double/debiased machine-learning theory provide the general cross-fitting remainder template.  Sommerfeld--Munk-type transport limits and second-order directional or first-order-degenerate delta methods motivate equality calibration, but the present negative result is limited to the unregularized full-tangent spectral route.
interpretation: The causal object of interest is the lower endpoint \(\theta_n\), not the generally unidentified moment \(E[\lVert Y_n(1)-Y_n(0)\rVert_2^2]\) itself.  The canonical gradient contains a covariate-composition term \(V_n(X)-\theta_n\) and one inverse-propensity centered transport derivative for the realized arm.  On a predetermined variance-separated collection with valid nuisance-rate premises, \(\widehat\theta_n\) is asymptotically linear with this influence function, \(\widehat\sigma_n\) consistently estimates its efficiency-bound standard deviation, and the two-sided interval \([\widehat\theta_n\mathbin\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_n/\sqrt n]\) has uniform limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  In a 401(k) SIPP application, this interpretation requires credible ignorability, overlap, support and Brenier regularity, nuisance learning rates, and variance separation.
technical_internal_limitation: The regular theorem is intentionally uniform only over predetermined \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\).  The variance-unrestricted parent \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\) admits conditional equality, where \(\theta_n=0\), \(\psi_n=0\), and the zero-denominator first-order pivot has exact Kolmogorov distance \(1/2\) from \(N(0,1)\).  The second variation is a weighted Neumann energy, and at an admissible equality law with nonatomic \(P_X\) the full-tangent Hessian has an infinite-dimensional identity compression, so it is not Hilbert--Schmidt.  This rules out a uniformly tight unregularized \(n\)-scale Gaussian spectral calibration over the full parent.  It does not rule out slower covariate-regularized, derivative-aware, subsampling, or other honest adaptive procedures; constructing and validating such a procedure remains open.
honest_scope: Sharp causal identification uses consistency, conditional ignorability, fixed overlap, and measurable attainment of the conditional optimal coupling.  Canonical-gradient validity is pointwise at regular-support laws in the full nonparametric observed-data tangent space.  Uniform root-\(n\) inference additionally requires a predetermined collection inside \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\), the stated support, density, and all-feasible-pairs Brenier conditions, and density and propensity learner rates imposed as estimator-side premises over that collection.  The primitive H\"older proposition verifies those rates only on \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs,H}}_{\sigma_\star,t_\pi,L_\pi}\).  No claim is made under hidden confounding, overlap failure, nonsmooth or unbounded supports, or for a single honest procedure uniformly adaptive across all positive-variance sequences and equality.  The degeneracy theorem is a partial route obstruction, not a solution of that broad open problem.
